title: Mukhyamantri Mahalakshmi Kit Yojana Uttarakhand
meta_description: Mukhyamantri Mahalakshmi Kit Yojana gives a free kit on birth of a girl child in Uttarakhand govt hospitals. Contents, eligibility, and how to get it.

hero.one_liner: Mukhyamantri Mahalakshmi Kit Yojana gives Uttarakhand mothers a free kit after the institutional delivery of a girl child, for the first two daughters.

what_is_it: Mukhyamantri Mahalakshmi Kit Yojana is an initiative of the Uttarakhand government to celebrate the birth of girl children and encourage mothers to deliver in government health facilities rather than at home. Launched in October 2020, the scheme addresses two interlinked goals: reducing the cultural bias against girl children that persists in parts of Uttarakhand, and improving maternal and infant health outcomes by incentivising institutional delivery where trained health workers are present.

The Mahalakshmi Kit is a carefully assembled box of essential items selected to meet the immediate practical needs of a newborn girl child and her mother in the first weeks after discharge from the hospital. The kit typically includes items the family might struggle to afford immediately after a birth: good-quality cotton clothing suited to a newborn, a warm woollen garment for Uttarakhand's cold hill climate, bathing and skincare products for the baby, and nutrition supplements for the mother who has just delivered.

how_to_apply.title: Deliver in a government health facility
how_to_apply.description: The Mahalakshmi Kit is given only at government hospitals, CHCs, PHCs, or sub-centres in Uttarakhand. Register for antenatal care at your nearest government health facility during pregnancy and plan to deliver there; your ASHA worker or ANM can help you identify the nearest facility.

how_to_apply.title: Inform the ANM or staff nurse about the girl child birth
how_to_apply.description: After delivery, health facility staff will record the birth details and the sex of the child. The facility's records trigger kit distribution automatically for girl child births; you do not need to apply separately or submit a special form to claim the kit.

how_to_apply.title: Receive the kit at discharge
how_to_apply.description: Before you are discharged from the health facility, the nursing staff or ASHA worker will present the Mahalakshmi Kit box along with any cash incentives due under JSY and discharge advice. Check that the kit is complete with all expected items before leaving the facility.

how_to_apply.title: Contact NHM if kit is unavailable
how_to_apply.description: If the health facility says the kit is out of stock or has not arrived, note the delivery date and facility name and contact the District Chief Medical Officer (CMO) or the District NHM Programme Officer to report the gap. The state NHM has obligations to maintain kit supply at all government delivery points.

extra_sections.heading: Inside Mahalakshmi Kit Yojana
content: The scheme has no income restriction, which makes it meaningfully different from most welfare schemes in India that require proof of Below Poverty Line (BPL) status or income certificates. Any woman who delivers a girl child in a government health facility in Uttarakhand, whether she is from a poor hill household or a middle-income family in the plains districts, receives the Mahalakshmi Kit; this universal approach maximises uptake and avoids the exclusion of genuinely needy families who lack the documentation to prove their poverty.

One of the central messages communicated through the Mahalakshmi Kit is symbolic: the government of Uttarakhand is publicly marking the birth of a girl child as an occasion for celebration rather than disappointment. The kit includes a welcome card from the government that celebrates the girl child's birth, reinforcing a message that challenges the historical preference for male children that has resulted in skewed sex ratios in several districts of Uttarakhand over the decades.

extra_sections.heading: Inside Mahalakshmi Kit Yojana: More Detail
content: The Mahalakshmi Kit Yojana is administered through the National Health Mission (NHM) Uttarakhand infrastructure, which means the kits are distributed through the existing network of district hospitals, community health centres (CHCs), primary health centres (PHCs), and sub-centres where government deliveries are conducted. ASHA workers and ANMs (Auxiliary Nurse Midwives) play a role in informing pregnant women about the scheme during antenatal checkups, ensuring that expectant mothers know the benefit awaiting them if they deliver a girl in a government facility.

The woollen frock included in the Mahalakshmi Kit is a thoughtful addition that reflects Uttarakhand's climatic reality: hill districts like Pithoragarh, Chamoli, Uttarkashi, and Rudraprayag can be extremely cold, and a newborn girl needs warm clothing regardless of the season. Many families in remote hill villages cannot afford to purchase warm baby clothes immediately after a delivery, and the inclusion of this item ensures that the girl child has protection against the cold during the critical early weeks of life.

extra_sections.title: A Kit for Mother and Newborn Girl
extra_sections.content:
Mahalakshmi Kit Yojana gives a free kit to a mother after the institutional delivery of a girl child. It supports the health and hygiene of mother and baby.

Launched by CM Pushkar Singh Dhami, it is a revised version of the earlier Soubhagyawati Yojana.

extra_sections.heading: The Headline Figures
content: The scheme supports Uttarakhand's broader maternal and child health goals under NHM by creating an additional incentive for institutional delivery specifically for girl child births. Institutional deliveries are safer than home births because trained professionals can manage complications, provide postnatal care, and ensure the newborn receives essential vaccinations; by linking the kit to government facility births, the scheme both rewards mothers who choose institutional delivery and provides a tangible reason for families to opt for it.

The iron-folic acid tablets and nutritional supplements included in the mother's portion of the Mahalakshmi Kit address the widespread problem of anaemia and nutritional deficiency among women in Uttarakhand's rural and hill areas. Postpartum anaemia is a major health risk for new mothers in India, and providing these supplements at the time of discharge from the hospital ensures that mothers have immediate access to the nutrition they need during the critical recovery period after childbirth.

extra_sections.heading: The Headline Figures: in Practice
content: The Mahalakshmi Kit Yojana operates in conjunction with other maternal health schemes including the Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY) and the Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY), which provide cash incentives for institutional deliveries. A mother who delivers a girl child in a government facility in Uttarakhand can receive JSY cash benefits, PMMVY maternity benefit instalments, and the Mahalakshmi Kit all through the same delivery event, creating a comprehensive support package that makes the decision to deliver in a government facility significantly more attractive.

District-level NHM teams in Uttarakhand are responsible for ensuring that adequate stocks of Mahalakshmi Kits are maintained at all government health facilities so that no eligible mother is turned away or asked to wait after delivering a girl child. The NHM Uttarakhand monitors kit distribution data across facilities and districts to track both coverage and any supply gaps that need to be addressed through timely procurement.

extra_sections.heading: Who the Scheme Covers
content: The Mahalakshmi Kit also serves as a data collection mechanism: every kit distributed is recorded by the health facility, generating a registry of girl child births in government facilities across Uttarakhand. This data is valuable for the state government's gender-sensitive planning, enabling officials to monitor the sex ratio at birth at the district and block level and identify areas where additional awareness or intervention may be needed to address persistent son preference.

Feedback from mothers and ASHA workers in Uttarakhand indicates that the Mahalakshmi Kit has been well received across hill and Tarai districts alike, with many families reporting that the kit's practical contents were genuinely useful in the first weeks after delivery. The scheme's framing as a celebration of the girl child has also been noted as meaningful by mothers who report that receiving the kit made them feel that the government was acknowledging and valuing their daughter's birth in a way that was new and affirming.

extra_sections.heading: Who the Scheme Covers: Key Points
content: The Mahalakshmi Kit Yojana reflects Uttarakhand's commitment to improving the sex ratio at birth, which has been a concern in the state because of historically male-biased cultural preferences in parts of both the Garhwal and Kumaon regions. The scheme works alongside awareness campaigns about the PCPNDT (Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques) Act and programmes against sex-selective practices, complementing legal enforcement with a positive incentive that makes the birth of a girl child associated with celebration and government support.

For families in the hill districts, the Mahalakshmi Kit provides immediate economic relief at a time when household expenses are typically elevated due to the birth event itself. The cost of purchasing equivalent quality baby clothing, hygiene products, and maternal supplements in a hill town shop would be significantly more than what most poor families can afford immediately after a delivery; the kit effectively transfers purchasing power to families at their moment of greatest need.

extra_sections.heading: Applying, Step by Step
content: The Uttarakhand government's communication around the Mahalakshmi Kit Yojana emphasises not just the material contents of the kit but its message: that daughters are as welcome and as worthy of celebration as sons. By distributing the kit through health facilities rather than welfare offices, the scheme integrates this positive messaging into a healthcare visit, reaching families at a moment when they are most open to health education and least likely to dismiss government communication as bureaucratic formality.

ASHA workers in Uttarakhand play a central role in making the Mahalakshmi Kit Yojana effective at the grassroots level. During home visits and antenatal camps, ASHAs inform pregnant women about the kit, encourage them to register for delivery at government facilities, and accompany them to the hospital for delivery; this facilitation role ensures that women in remote villages who might not otherwise know about the scheme or feel confident going to a hospital are guided through the process with support.

extra_sections.title: Institutional Delivery Is a Must
extra_sections.content:
The kit is given only after an institutional delivery at a hospital, not a home birth. This is a firm condition of the scheme.

Register at the Anganwadi during pregnancy so your details are ready when you collect the kit.

extra_sections.heading: Applying, Step by Step: Key Points
content: The Mahalakshmi Kit Yojana has been noted as an important complement to the state's Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP) campaign, which works to improve child sex ratios and girls' access to education in Uttarakhand's lower-performing districts. Where BBBP awareness campaigns change attitudes over time, the Mahalakshmi Kit provides an immediate, tangible reinforcement of the same message at the most critical moment: the birth of a girl child in a family that has chosen to deliver in a government hospital.

For first-time mothers from hill families, the Mahalakshmi Kit often introduces them to products and practices they may not have encountered before, such as commercial baby soap formulated for sensitive skin, standardised nutrition supplements, and hygienic feeding utensils. The kit thus has an educational dimension alongside its welfare purpose: it exposes new mothers to better infant care practices at a teachable moment and health facility staff can explain the appropriate use of each item at discharge.

extra_sections.title: For the First Two Daughters
extra_sections.desc:
The kit is given for the first two girl children of a mother. In the case of twin girls, the mother gets one kit and each newborn gets a separate kit.

The aim is to encourage safe institutional deliveries and welcome the girl child.

extra_sections.heading: The Fine Print on Eligibility
content: The kit's inclusion of a woollen frock for the baby girl is especially significant given Uttarakhand's climate. Many hill district temperatures drop severely in winter, and a newborn girl child in a poor household may not have warm clothing unless provided by the government or relatives; the woollen garment in the kit addresses this vulnerability directly, ensuring the baby's first weeks outside the hospital are not spent in inadequately warm clothing during Uttarakhand's cold months.

The government's decision to include maternal items like a saree or dupatta alongside the baby items in the Mahalakshmi Kit is a deliberate acknowledgement that the mother herself is a beneficiary of the scheme, not merely a carrier of the girl child who deserves support. By including something specifically for the mother, the scheme recognises her experience and dignity and signals that the government's celebration of the girl child birth extends to honouring the mother who delivered her.

extra_sections.heading: The Fine Print on Eligibility: The Specifics
content: Uttarakhand's sex ratio at birth has shown improvement over recent years, and schemes like the Mahalakshmi Kit Yojana are credited by state health officials as one factor contributing to this positive trend. While causality is difficult to establish in isolation, the combination of positive incentives for girl child births at government facilities, enforcement of PCPNDT rules, and BBBP awareness campaigns has created a multi-pronged environment that discourages sex-selective practices and rewards the safe delivery of girl children.

The Mahalakshmi Kit Yojana also helps build long-term trust between hill communities and the government health system. A family that received the kit at their daughter's birth is more likely to return to the same facility for the daughter's vaccination schedule and subsequent deliveries; this trust-building effect compounds over time and contributes to the broader goal of increasing utilisation of government health services in rural and hill Uttarakhand.

extra_sections.title: Register Early in Pregnancy
extra_sections.content:
Register at your Anganwadi Centre early, so there is no last-minute paperwork after delivery.

The Anganwadi worker can also guide you on the nearest hospital for a safe institutional delivery.

extra_sections.heading: The Paperwork
content: The scheme creates a virtuous cycle for girl child health outcomes that extends well beyond the immediate newborn period and the hospital stay. A mother who delivers in a government facility and receives the Mahalakshmi Kit is typically briefed by health facility staff about the child immunisation schedule under the Universal Immunisation Programme (UIP), making it considerably more likely that the girl child will receive all required vaccines in her first two years of life, thereby reducing preventable illness and childhood mortality across the state's hill and rural communities.

The Mahalakshmi Kit Yojana works in synergy with the Mukhyamantri Mahalakshmi Yojana (a maternity benefit scheme) and other state welfare programmes to create a layered, comprehensive package of support for mothers delivering girl children in Uttarakhand. Each scheme in this constellation addresses a different dimension of the mother-daughter welfare equation: cash support, in-kind product support, healthcare access, and positive social messaging work collectively to achieve outcomes that no single scheme operating in isolation could accomplish on its own.

extra_sections.title: The Paperwork Notes
extra_sections.content:
Community-level impact data collected by NHM Uttarakhand and district health teams has shown that in blocks where Mahalakshmi Kit distribution has been consistent and well-publicised, the percentage of women choosing government facilities for delivery has increased, and family attitudes toward girl children have shown measurable improvement in participatory health and gender assessment surveys. These encouraging findings strongly support the continuation and further expansion of the scheme as a proven, cost-effective tool for simultaneously improving institutional delivery rates and transforming gender attitudes in Uttarakhand's communities.

The Mahalakshmi Kit Yojana stands as evidence that welfare policies can carry multiple functions at once: providing immediate material relief, incentivising health-promoting behaviour, building institutional trust, and delivering a cultural message that fundamentally reframes how communities think about the birth of daughters. For a state like Uttarakhand, where the difficult terrain makes service delivery challenging and deep-rooted cultural attitudes change slowly, the scheme represents a practical, dignified, and cost-effective approach to advancing both maternal health outcomes and gender equality goals simultaneously across all 13 districts.

extra_sections.heading: The Bigger Picture
content: For families in remote hill villages where the nearest government health facility may require hours of travel on difficult mountain roads, the decision to pursue institutional delivery for a girl child involves real cost and effort. The Mahalakshmi Kit helps offset these costs by providing a meaningful benefit that the family receives immediately upon delivery; when families calculate that the kit plus JSY cash plus postnatal care add up to significant support, the financial and practical calculus shifts in favour of institutional delivery.

The NHM Uttarakhand tracks Mahalakshmi Kit distribution as a key performance indicator in its district health reporting system, and districts that show gaps in kit supply or low distribution rates are expected to provide explanations and remediation plans to the state health directorate. This accountability mechanism ensures that the scheme is not just a policy announcement but an operationally tracked intervention that state health management actively monitors to ensure no eligible mother is left without her kit.

extra_sections.title: In Their Words Notes
extra_sections.content: The Mahalakshmi Kit is more than a box of baby items. It is the Uttarakhand government's official welcome to every girl child born in a government hospital, a tangible statement that daughters are valued and that the state stands behind them from the moment of their birth.

faqs.question: What is Mukhyamantri Mahalakshmi Kit Yojana?
faqs.answer: It is an Uttarakhand government scheme that provides a free kit of baby and maternal items worth approximately Rs 2,000-2,500 to every mother who delivers a girl child in a government health facility in Uttarakhand. The scheme aims to celebrate girl child births and encourage institutional delivery.

faqs.question: Who is eligible for the Mahalakshmi Kit?
faqs.answer:
Any woman who delivers a girl child in a government hospital, CHC, PHC, or sub-centre in Uttarakhand is eligible. There is no income limit or BPL requirement.

The only conditions are that the delivery must be in a government facility and the child must be a girl.

faqs.question: What items are included in the Mahalakshmi Kit?
faqs.answer:
The kit includes items for both the baby girl and the mother. Baby items include cotton frocks, a woollen frock, cotton nappies, a blanket, mosquito net, baby soap, baby oil, and a towel.

Maternal items include a saree or dupatta, iron-folic acid tablets, nutritional supplements, sanitary pads, and a feeding cup or bowl, along with a welcome card from the government.

faqs.question: When is the Mahalakshmi Kit given?
faqs.answer: The kit is given at the time of discharge from the government health facility after delivery. You do not need to apply separately; the health facility staff records the girl child birth and hands over the kit before you leave.

faqs.question: Do I need to apply for the Mahalakshmi Kit?
faqs.answer:
No. There is no separate application process. When you deliver a girl child in a government health facility, the staff automatically records the birth and provides the kit at discharge.

If the facility does not provide the kit, you can contact the District CMO or District NHM Officer.

faqs.question: Is the Mahalakshmi Kit available for home deliveries?
faqs.answer:
No. The scheme is specifically designed to encourage institutional delivery. Only mothers who deliver in government health facilities (hospitals, CHCs, PHCs, sub-centres) are eligible.

Home deliveries are not covered.

faqs.question: Can I get the Mahalakshmi Kit for my second or third girl child?
faqs.answer: The scheme provides the kit for girl child births in government facilities and the scheme guidelines primarily target institutional births. Check with your local government health facility or ASHA worker for the current rules on multiple births under the scheme.

faqs.question: Does the Mahalakshmi Kit come with any cash benefit?
faqs.answer: The Mahalakshmi Kit itself is a product kit, not a cash transfer. However, mothers delivering in government facilities in Uttarakhand can also receive cash benefits under the Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) and the Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY), which operate alongside the Mahalakshmi Kit scheme.

faqs.question: What if the kit is not available at my health facility?
faqs.answer: If the health facility says the kit is out of stock, note your delivery date and facility name and contact the District Chief Medical Officer (CMO) or District NHM Programme Officer to report the shortage. The NHM Uttarakhand is responsible for ensuring kit supply at all government delivery points across the state.

faqs.question: Where can I get more information about the Mahalakshmi Kit Yojana?
faqs.answer: Information is available at nhm.uk.gov.in (NHM Uttarakhand's official website), your nearest government hospital or CHC, or through your ASHA worker or ANM who can explain the scheme during antenatal visits.
